Vehicle recovery · breakdown · transport & salvage

Recovery & breakdown truck graphics.

Your truck turns up when someone is stuck at the roadside. Clear, professional graphics that show who you are and how to call you, day or night, without borrowing anyone else’s livery.

DISCUSS YOUR RECOVERY VEHICLES ↗CALL 01603 407786

Norwich workshop · NR6 6AQ · Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5pm

Vehicle graphics / Sectors / Automotive / Recovery & breakdown truck graphics
What it needs to sayWhat goes whereOptions & pricesPractical pointsWhat to send usProcessFAQsDiscuss your vehicles ↗

Seen at the worst moment. Remembered after.

A recovery truck is often first seen by someone having a bad day: a stranded driver, a dealer waiting for a delivery, a garage expecting a non-runner. The graphics have to inspire confidence quickly. A clear name, “24-hour recovery” or the hours you work, and a phone number large enough to read from a lay-by or across a car park.

Recovery work is also repeat business with trade customers. Garages, dealers, fleet managers and insurers remember the operator who turned up promptly in a smart truck. Consistent livery across the fleet helps them recognise you, and makes it easy to add vehicles later.

Typical vehicles. Slide-bed and tilt-and-slide recovery trucks, spectacle-lift trucks, car transporters, and support vans for jump starts and fuel deliveries. The body, cab, headboard and beavertail each offer different panels, so we plan around the truck’s actual build.

What goes where.

Layout

Name on the cab. Number everywhere.

The cab doors are seen at eye level and suit the name and logo. The sides of the bed or body give a long, low strip that works well for the name and phone number. The headboard, seen over the cab from behind, is a good place for the phone number in very large lettering.

Cab doorsName, logo and operator details
Bed / body sidesName, services and phone
HeadboardPhone number, large
RearPhone and any markings your clients require

Beds, ramps and winch areas get scraped by straps, wheels and chains. We keep graphics off those working surfaces so they last.

From cab lettering to fleet livery.

Recovery trucks vary too much for a fixed price, so we quote them from photographs and measurements. Our published supply-and-fit van packages apply to van-based support vehicles fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. All prices are “from”, + VAT, and confirmed by quote.

Support vans, from £149 + VAT ↗

Basic cut-vinyl name and contact details from £149 + VAT; Standard adds a logo and second colour from £210 + VAT.

Reflective graphics ↗

Bespoke cut reflective lettering and panels made on our drag-knife and laser cutters. Quoted to your design.

Fleet livery ↗

One design adapted to each truck, transporter and van so the fleet matches. Quoted per vehicle.

Chapter 8 chevron kits ↗

Rear chevron kits for most mainstream vehicles, or bespoke cut reflectives, where your work or client requires them.

Read Chapter 8 chevrons explained for the general background, and see fleet graphics for rollouts across several vehicles.

Practical points for recovery operators.

Do not copy emergency-service livery. Battenburg-style chequer patterns and markings that make a vehicle look like police, ambulance or fire service are restricted, and we will not produce designs that imitate them. A recovery truck should look like a recovery truck.

Check the rules for markings. Rear chevrons, reflective materials and their colours and positions are covered by current regulations and guidance, and by the requirements of clients such as motoring organisations, police removal schemes and highways contractors. Get their specification first; we produce to it.

Beacons and lights. Warning beacons and lighting have their own rules and are separate from the graphics. We keep vinyl clear of lamps, reflectors and number plates.

Night visibility. Reflective lettering can help your name and number be seen in headlights. Ask us to show reflective and standard options side by side.

What to send us.

Trucks are quoted from good information. Please send:

  • Chassis make and model, body builder and body type for each vehicle.
  • Photographs of the cab, both sides of the body, headboard and rear.
  • Any client or contract specifications for markings and reflectives.
  • Your logo files and the exact wording, including hours and phone numbers.
  • How many vehicles, and whether new ones are due soon.
  • Whether vehicles can come to our workshop, or need on-site fitting (quoted separately).

SEND YOUR TRUCK DETAILS ↗

A clear process. From start to finish.

01

Gather the spec.

Send photographs, wording and any client requirements so the design starts from the rules that apply to you.

02

Approve the fleet design.

We adapt the livery to each vehicle type and send proofs for you to check together.

03

Produce in-house.

Printed on our 8-colour, 1440dpi printers, with lettering and reflectives cut in-house from 3M and Metamark materials.

We agree fitting dates around your call-outs and fit at our Norwich workshop.

Recovery trucks are quoted individually from photographs and measurements. Van-based support vehicles start from £149 + VAT for Basic supply-and-fit graphics within 30 miles of our Norwich workshop. Your quote confirms the price.

Can we use chequer or battenburg patterns?

No. Those markings are associated with the emergency services and their use is restricted. We will design high-visibility graphics that are clearly your own.

Do we need rear chevrons?

That depends on the work you do, current rules and your clients’ requirements. Check with them and the current guidance; we supply Chapter 8 kits and bespoke reflectives once you know what is needed.

Can graphics cope with the bed and ramps?

Working surfaces take heavy wear, so we keep graphics off them and onto body panels, the cab and the headboard. Damaged panels can be replaced individually.

html:
Removals · storage · house clearance · man & van

Removals van graphics.

A removals lorry is a giant flat billboard parked outside a sold house. Use that space to earn the next move.

DISCUSS YOUR VEHICLES ↗CALL 01603 407786

Norwich workshop · NR6 6AQ · Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5pm

Vehicle graphics / Sectors / Logistics & transport / Removals van graphics
Earning trustWhat goes whereOptions & pricesPractical pointsWhat to send usProcessFAQsDiscuss your vehicles ↗

Trusted with everything they own.

Choosing a removals firm is a nervous decision. People are handing over their furniture, their heirlooms and often a fixed completion date to a company they may never have used before. Many start by asking neighbours, friends or their estate agent, and they remember the firms they have seen on moving day: the smart lorry outside a house down the road, the crew carrying a piano without fuss. Removals graphics should look calm, established and careful as much as they look eye-catching.

The essentials are a well-presented name and logo, a clear statement of what you do (“Home & office removals”, “Removals & storage”, “Packing services”), and contact details large enough to note from across the street. A smaller line naming the area you cover helps customers judge whether you are local. Any membership, insurance or accreditation claims should be ones you can back up.

Typical vehicles are Luton box vans, 7.5-tonne box lorries, larger pantechnicons and the vans used for surveys and small moves. Storage firms may also want containers and trailers branded to match.

What goes where.

Layout

Use the box. Keep it simple.

Box bodies offer some of the largest flat panels on any vehicle. That makes them ideal for a bold printed design, but a big panel still needs a clear hierarchy, or the phone number gets lost in a picture of a house.

Box sidesLogo, name, services line and large contact details
Luton peakName, read by traffic ahead and from upstairs windows
Rear & tail liftPhone number and web address, clear of lights and markings
Cab doorsName and logo

Rows of rivets, rubbing strips and the side door on some bodies break up the panel. We plan the layout so key words do not fall across them.

From lettering to a printed box.

Survey vans and smaller removals vans can use our published supply-and-fit packages, fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. Box lorries and printed boxes are quoted for the vehicle. All prices are “from” and + VAT, confirmed by quote.

Van packages, from £149 + VAT ↗

Basic from £149, Standard from £210 and Pro from £455, all + VAT, for survey and small-move vans.

Box lorry livery ↗

Cut vinyl and printed panels on cab and box, designed to match your vans and paperwork.

Full box wraps ↗

Full-colour printed coverage of the box sides and rear. Quoted for the body size and artwork.

Fleet & storage ↗

One look across vans, lorries, trailers and storage containers.

Running a single man-and-van? Supply-only van graphics in our online shop start from £95 + VAT.

Practical points for removals firms.

Big panels, joined neatly. Our printers print roughly 1.5m wide by up to 50m long, so a large box side is printed in panels and joined. We plan the joins so they fall in sensible places rather than through a face or a phone number.

Roller shutters. Shutter slats roll and flex, which is hard on vinyl. Where a body has a shutter, the main graphics are usually best kept to the fixed panels around it.

Claims on the van. Customers take “fully insured” or a trade association logo at face value. Only show what you can evidence, and use official logo artwork under each scheme’s rules.

Box condition. Older GRP and aluminium boxes can be chalky, scratched or patched. Send close-up photographs, as surface condition affects how well, and how long, a wrap will perform.

What to send us.

For removals vehicles, please gather:

  • Make, model and body type of each vehicle, with box length and height if known.
  • Photographs of both box sides, the Luton peak, the rear and the cab doors.
  • Close-ups of rivet lines, rubbing strips, shutters or side doors.
  • Your logo as a vector file, and any photographs you want used, at full resolution.
  • Exact wording: name, services, areas covered, phone number and web address.
  • Any membership or accreditation logos you are entitled to use, in official artwork.

SEND YOUR VEHICLE DETAILS ↗

A clear process. From start to finish.

01

Show us the vehicles.

Send photographs and dimensions. Our in-house design department can develop the design or work with yours.

02

Approve the box layout.

We mock the design up on your body, showing where panel joins, rivets and shutters fall.

03

Print large.

Panels are printed on our 8-colour, 1440dpi printers using 3M and Metamark materials.

Fit between moves.

We agree a fitting date around your bookings, so the vehicle is ready for the next move.

Can you wrap the whole box on a removals lorry?

Yes. Large boxes are printed in panels and joined, and we plan the joins around the design. The price depends on the box size, its condition and the artwork, and is confirmed by quote.

Is cut lettering or a printed wrap better for removals?

Cut vinyl lettering is cost-effective and very clear. A printed box gives more impact and room for imagery. Many firms use printed boxes on lorries and simpler lettering on vans; our wrap or part graphics comparison explains the trade-offs.

Can you brand storage containers too?

Send photographs and sizes of the containers. If the surface is sound and clean, vinyl graphics can match the vehicles; we will advise on the best positions.

Vans fitted within 30 miles of Norwich start from £149 + VAT (Basic), £210 + VAT (Standard) and £455 + VAT (Pro). Box lorries and wraps are quoted individually.

Shops · showrooms · garden centres · online retailers

Retail delivery van graphics.

Every delivery ends at a customer’s front door, often in sight of their neighbours. Make sure the van carries the shop with it.

DISCUSS YOUR DELIVERY VAN ↗CALL 01603 407786

Norwich workshop · NR6 6AQ · Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5pm

Vehicle graphics / Sectors / Retail & local services / Retail delivery vans
What shoppers readWhat goes whereOptions & pricesPractical pointsWhat to send usProcessFAQsDiscuss your van ↗

Your shop, on every street you deliver to.

A delivery van does a different job from a trade van. Nobody books a furniture shop or a farm shop because they saw the van; they remember it next time they need a sofa, a bag of compost or a Sunday joint. The graphics should make the business instantly recognisable as the shop people already know, and remind them how to buy again.

That means matching the shopfront. Use the same logo, colours and typeface as the fascia, bags and website, so the van reads as part of the same brand. Then add the two things a shopper needs: where to buy (“Visit our showroom on…” or the web address for online orders) and what you sell, in a few plain words. A delivery promise such as “Local delivery available” is worth adding if it is true for your area.

Delivery vans are also seen while they wait: double-parked for a few minutes, reversed onto a drive, or loading at the back of the shop. Customers and passers-by have time to read the rear and the kerb side properly.

Typical vehicles.

Small vans such as a Caddy or Berlingo for florists, pharmacies and gift shops; medium panel vans for hardware, appliance and bed shops; Luton box vans with tail lifts for furniture and white goods; and refrigerated vans for butchers, farm shops and grocers. Box bodies give large, flat panels that suit printed photography of your products.

What goes where.

Layout

Brand on the sides. How to buy on the back.

On a panel van, the sides carry the shop name and logo, sized to match the shopfront. On a Luton, the box sides are effectively a moving poster, so this is where product photography or a strong brand colour pays off. The rear is read by the traffic behind and by the customer watching their delivery come off the tail lift.

Box or panel sidesShop name, logo and what you sell
Cab doorsAddress or “Visit our showroom”
RearWeb address and phone number, large and simple

Roller shutters flex at every slat, so we usually keep lettering on the solid panels around them. Tail-lift and conversion markings fitted by the body builder should stay visible, and we plan around refrigeration units, vents and step plates.

From basic lettering to a full wrap.

Panel vans can use our published supply-and-fit packages, fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. Prices are “from” and + VAT, and your quote confirms the figure. Luton and refrigerated box bodies are quoted for the size of the body.

Basic graphics, from £149 + VAT ↗

Single-colour shop name on the bonnet, sides and rear, with phone and web address low down. A tidy start for a small delivery van.

Standard graphics, from £210 + VAT ↗

Adds your logo, a second colour or panel infill and social media details, so the van matches the shop’s colours.

Pro graphics, from £455 + VAT ↗

Up to three design ideas beyond the standard layout, with a large logo or graphic on the rear quarters and rear.

Box bodies & wraps ↗

Printed product photography across a Luton box or a full panel-van wrap, quoted for your vehicle and artwork.

Running several delivery vans? Our fleet graphics page covers keeping livery consistent as vans are replaced. If you are updating the shopfront too, our signage team can work from the same artwork.

Practical points for delivery vans.

Match the shop exactly. Send colour references (Pantone or the values your sign maker or printer used) so the van, fascia and carrier bags agree. Colours on a phone screen are not a reliable guide.

Keep offers separate. Sales and seasonal offers change; your name does not. Put promotions on a separate vinyl panel that can be removed and replaced without touching the permanent graphics.

Chilled and box bodies. Insulated and GRP box bodies behave differently from steel panels. Tell us who built the body and send photographs of seams, rivets and any manufacturer labels.

Out after dark. Winter deliveries often run into the evening. Light lettering on a dark van, or a reflective element on the rear, helps the van be read under street lights.

What to send us.

Send these and we can price the van quickly and accurately:

  • Make, model and year, and for box vans the body length and builder.
  • Photographs of every side, including the tail lift, shutter and any fridge unit.
  • Your logo as a vector file and your shop’s colour references.
  • The wording: shop name, what you sell, address or showroom line, phone and web address.
  • Any product photographs you want to use, at full resolution.
  • How many vans, and whether they should all match.

SEND YOUR VAN DETAILS ↗

A clear process. From start to finish.

01

Brief us.

Send photographs, wording and logo files. Our in-house design department can adapt your shop branding for the van.

02

Approve the layout.

We draw the design on your van or box body so you can check positions, colours and spelling.

03

Print and cut.

Graphics are printed on our 8-colour, 1440dpi printers or cut from in-stock vinyl, using 3M and Metamark materials.

04

Fit and collect.

We fit at the Norwich workshop on a date that suits your delivery schedule, and explain aftercare when you collect.

Your questions. Answered.

How much do delivery van graphics cost?

For panel vans fitted within 30 miles of our Norwich workshop, packages start from £149 + VAT (Basic), from £210 + VAT (Standard) and from £455 + VAT (Pro). Box bodies and wraps are quoted. Your quote confirms the final price.

Can you match our shopfront colours?

Yes, as closely as the materials allow. Send the colour references used for your signage or print, and we will choose a coloured vinyl or print the colour to match.

Can we advertise a seasonal sale on the van?

Yes. Keep the offer on its own removable panel so it can come off after the sale without disturbing the shop name and contact details.

Will graphics work on a refrigerated van?

Usually, but insulated bodies vary. Tell us the body builder and send photographs so we can check the surface, seams and labels before quoting.

Arrive looking like the business you are.

For shops and local service businesses, the vehicle is often the only part of the business a customer sees in person. A florist’s van at the door, a mobile groomer parked on the drive, a stylist’s car outside a client’s home: each sets expectations before anyone knocks.

The vehicles range from small cars to long-wheelbase vans, and the messages differ. A retailer wants the shop’s look carried onto the street. A mobile service wants to show what it does and how to book. A security firm or an IT engineer needs to look official, trustworthy and easy to identify, without overstating what they are.

Most businesses in this group already have a shopfront, website or uniform. Matching the vehicle to that identity is usually the starting point; if you also need shop or window signs, see our signage service.

Options and prices.

Cars and vans

Match the shop, the site and the van.

A single van can start with clear lettering and your logo. Printed panels or a part wrap carry more of a shop’s colour and imagery, and suit businesses whose product sells on looks, such as flowers or grooming.

For vans fitted within 30 miles of our Norwich workshop, the published packages below apply; car graphics follow the same structure. Prices are “from” and + VAT, confirmed by quotation.

Practical points for local services.

Security livery. Do not use designs, colours or words that could be mistaken for the police or another emergency service: battenburg-style patterns are restricted, and we will not copy them. Check any requirements from your licensing body or clients before approving artwork.

Client branding. Engineers working for a network operator or retailer may be asked to carry the client’s brand. Ask for the client’s guidelines and approval process before we design.

Removable for personal cars. Mobile stylists often use their own car. Vinyl is semi-permanent and can be removed, so door graphics can come off if the car is sold.

Seasonal messages. Florists and retailers can keep the brand permanent and add smaller seasonal panels that are changed for busy periods.

Groomers and water. Mobile grooming vans have water tanks, hoses and waste outlets. Mark them on your photographs so graphics stay clear of fittings and areas that are often wet.

We fit at the Norwich workshop on an agreed date and explain aftercare when you collect.

What to send us.

  • The make and model of the car or van, with photographs of each side and the rear.
  • Your logo, colours and photographs of your shopfront or website.
  • The exact wording: name, service line, phone, web address and social handles.
  • For security or subcontract work, any client or licensing requirements and the approved wording.
  • Whether the vehicle is your own, leased or a company car.
  • Whether we should fit the graphics or post a supply-only kit for you to apply.

Your questions. Answered.

Can you put graphics on my own car and take them off later?

Yes. Vehicle graphics are semi-permanent. On sound factory paint, quality vinyl usually comes away cleanly when you sell or change the car.

Can a security van use blue and yellow squares?

No. Battenburg-style and other emergency-service markings are restricted, and we will not reproduce them. We design high-visibility branding that is clearly your company’s own.

Can you match the van to our shopfront?

Yes. Send photographs of the shop and your brand files, and our design team will carry the same look onto the vehicle.

Do you letter vans for subcontractors carrying a client’s brand?

Yes, provided the client has approved it. Send their guidelines and artwork, and confirm who signs off the proof.

How much do graphics for a delivery van cost?

For a van fitted within 30 miles of Norwich, packages run from £149 + VAT (Basic) through £210 + VAT (Standard) to £455 + VAT (Pro). The final price is confirmed by quotation.

html:
Scaffolders · access contractors · temporary works

Scaffolding vehicle graphics.

Your lorry is parked outside for the whole erection and strike. Let everyone walking past know whose scaffold it is.

DISCUSS YOUR LORRIES ↗CALL 01603 407786

Norwich workshop · NR6 6AQ · Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5pm

Vehicle graphics / Sectors / Construction & plant / Scaffolding vehicle graphics
Who sees itWhat goes whereOptions & pricesPractical pointsWhat to send usProcessFAQsDiscuss your lorries ↗

The street is your showroom.

Scaffolding work is unusually public. On a domestic job the lorry sits at the kerb while the gang carries tube and boards up the drive, and the neighbours watch every lift. On a commercial site it is lined up beside the builder’s and roofer’s vehicles at the gate. Many scaffolding firms win work from exactly these moments: a homeowner planning a loft conversion, a roofer looking for a reliable firm, a builder whose usual scaffolder has let them down.

So the lorry needs to tell people three things quickly: that you are a scaffolding company, the name to remember, and a number to ring. A description such as “Domestic & commercial scaffolding”, “Temporary roofs” or “Access solutions” helps a passer-by judge whether you do the kind of job they have in mind.

Typical vehicles are flatbed and dropside lorries in a range of sizes, often with a tall headboard behind the cab, plus crew vans and pickups for smaller jobs and inspections. Lorries are worked hard, loaded with steel every day, and rarely clean for long, which shapes both the design and where it goes.

What goes where.

Layout

Cab for the name. Sideboards for the number.

Once a scaffolding lorry is loaded, tube and boards hide much of the bed and often overhang the rear. The cab and the outside of the body are what stay visible, so that is where the key information belongs.

Cab doorsCompany name and logo
Sideboards & bodyServices line and a large phone number
Headboard & cab frontName or logo, read by oncoming traffic and on site

Ribbed or corrugated dropsides are a poor surface for lettering, because vinyl cannot follow every ridge. Flat panels, or a flat board fixed to the body, give a far better result. Send photographs and we will suggest what will work.

From cab lettering to full livery.

Lorries are quoted for the vehicle and design. The crew vans and pickups can use our published supply-and-fit packages, fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. Prices are “from” and + VAT; your quote confirms the figure.

Basic van graphics, from £149 + VAT ↗

Single-colour name to bonnet, sides and rear, with phone and web details low on the sides and rear doors.

Standard & Pro, from £210 + VAT ↗

Standard adds a second colour and logo; Pro, from £455 + VAT, adds design ideas and larger rear graphics.

Lorry livery ↗

Cab, headboard and body graphics designed to match your vans, so the whole yard looks like one company.

Cab & van wraps ↗

Printed or colour-change coverage for a cab or van. Quoted for your vehicle and artwork.

Want to fit the van lettering yourself? Supply-only van graphics are in our online shop from £95 + VAT.

Practical points for scaffolding firms.

Loads and the rear. Projecting loads and rear markings are covered by rules on vehicle lighting and load marking. Check the current requirements for your vehicles and keep any required markings, plates and lights clear of graphics. Do not rely on rear lettering being visible once the lorry is loaded.

Wear and tear. Tube is dragged across sideboards and headboards every day. Keep lettering away from the top edges and corners where steel lands, and accept that the most exposed panels will need refreshing sooner. Semi-permanent vinyl means a single damaged panel can be replaced on its own.

Match the scaffold. Many firms also brand the scaffold itself with banners and boards. If you want the same artwork on site signage, our signage team works from the same files.

Accreditations. Show only the scheme and trade body logos you are entitled to use, from official artwork, following each scheme’s own rules.

What to send us.

For scaffolding lorries and support vehicles, please include:

  • Make, model and body type of each vehicle (flatbed, dropside, crew van, pickup).
  • Photographs of the cab, both sides of the body, the headboard and the rear, unloaded.
  • Close-ups of the sideboards so we can see whether they are flat or ribbed.
  • Your logo as a vector file, and any colours you use on banners or workwear.
  • Exact wording: name, services line, phone number and web address.
  • Any accreditation logos you are entitled to show, in official artwork.

SEND YOUR VEHICLE DETAILS ↗

A clear process. From start to finish.

01

Photograph the fleet.

Send pictures of each vehicle, unloaded. No logo yet? Our in-house design department can create one.

02

See it on your lorry.

We lay the design out on your vehicle outline so you can check sizes and positions on cab, body and headboard.

03

Produce in-house.

Lettering is cut or printed in Norwich on 3M and Metamark materials, with plenty of coloured vinyl in stock.

04

Fit around your week.

Vans are fitted at our workshop on an agreed date; ask about courtesy vehicles while a van is off the road.

Your questions. Answered.

Can you put graphics on aluminium dropsides?

On flat aluminium panels, yes. Ribbed or corrugated sides are much harder because the vinyl has to bridge or follow every ridge. Send close-up photographs and we will suggest the best position, or a flat panel for the lettering.

Will the graphics survive tube being loaded?

Graphics placed away from the top edges and corners last far better. Some wear is inevitable on a working lorry, but semi-permanent vinyl means a scuffed section can be replaced without redoing the whole vehicle.

Do you do lorries as well as vans?

Yes. Our range runs from simple lettering up to a full colour-change wrap on a 56-seater coach, and our printers handle large-vehicle graphics. Lorries are quoted individually.

How much do scaffolding van graphics cost?

Van packages start from £149 + VAT (Basic), £210 + VAT (Standard) and £455 + VAT (Pro), fitted within 30 miles of Norwich. Lorries and wraps are quoted, and every price is confirmed by quote.

html:
Schools · academies · colleges

School minibus graphics.

A school minibus is a familiar sight to parents and the local community. Well-planned graphics make it look cared for, while keeping required signs, exits and the driver’s view clear.

DISCUSS YOUR MINIBUS ↗CALL 01603 407786

Norwich workshop · NR6 6AQ · Monday–Friday, 8:30am–5pm

Vehicle graphics / Sectors / Health, care & public sector / School minibus graphics
Your school on the roadWhat goes whereOptions & pricesSafety & signsWhat to send usProcessFAQsDiscuss your minibus ↗

Your school, on the road.

School and college minibuses carry pupils to fixtures, trips, swimming lessons and work placements, and spend the rest of the time parked where parents, prospective families and neighbours see them. The livery is part of the school’s identity, like the sign at the gate or the uniform, so it should match your crest or logo and colours.

The essentials are short: the school or trust name, the crest, and perhaps a web address. A minibus doesn’t need a long list of details the way a trade van does, though some schools add the office number to the rear so other road users have someone to contact. A motto, a sports-team mark or a sponsor can follow if there is room.

Most importantly, a minibus carrying children comes with responsibilities of its own. Any signs you are required to show, emergency exit markings, seating and accessibility labels and the driver’s view all come before branding. We design around them, never over them.

What goes where.

Layout

Identity on the sides. Safety at the back.

On a minibus the sides are long and broken by windows, so the school name usually runs along the panel below the window line, with the crest towards the front. The rear doors are where safety signs and exit markings are often found, so plan that space first.

Sides, below the windowsSchool or trust name and crest
Front doors or bonnetCrest or short name
RearSpace kept for required signs and exit markings, then a web address

Graphics on passenger windows are possible, but they reduce light inside and can affect what the driver sees in the mirrors. We usually recommend keeping the glass clear unless there is a specific reason.

From a name strip to full school colours.

Minibuses are larger than the vans our published packages are built around, so every minibus is quoted individually. As a guide to where prices start, these are our van supply-and-fit packages, fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. All prices are “from” and + VAT, confirmed by quote.

Basic graphics, from £149 + VAT (vans) ↗

Single-colour cut vinyl name on the bonnet, sides and rear, with details on the lower panels. The starting point for a simple name strip.

Standard graphics, from £210 + VAT (vans) ↗

Adds a cut or printed crest and a second colour or panel infill, subject to complexity and hi-res files.

Pro graphics, from £455 + VAT (vans) ↗

Design options beyond the standard layout, up to three ideas, with larger graphics on the rear quarters and rear.

Part & full wraps ↗

School colours across the whole vehicle, or printed panels on the sides. Quoted for your minibus.

Our work ranges from simple lettering up to a full colour-change wrap on a 56-seater coach, so larger school buses can be quoted in the same way. Send photographs of every side with your enquiry.

Safety, signs and rules.

Check the current rules. What a school minibus must display can depend on how it is used and who operates it. Check the current guidance with your local authority, trust or transport provider before ordering, and send us anything you are told to show. We can’t tell you which rules apply to your vehicle.

Keep required markings visible. Emergency exit labels, safety notices and any required signs must stay clear and readable. Send photographs of every existing label so the layout avoids them.

Safeguarding. Check your safeguarding policy before using photographs of pupils, or anything that identifies individual children, on the outside of the vehicle.

Nothing emergency-style. Reflective chequers or blue-and-yellow patterns might look like a safety feature, but emergency-service markings are restricted and can mislead other road users. We won’t produce them for a school minibus; your school colours do the job.

Plan around term. Fitting during a holiday keeps the minibus available in term. Tell us your dates when you enquire.

What to send us.

To quote for school minibus graphics, send:

  • The make, model, year, length and roof height of the minibus.
  • Photographs of both sides, the front and the rear, showing existing signs and exit labels.
  • Your crest or logo in vector format, and your brand colours.
  • The wording: school or trust name, and any web address, motto or sponsor.
  • Anything your local authority, trust or transport provider says must be displayed.
  • Your purchase order process and the dates the minibus can be off the road.

SEND YOUR MINIBUS DETAILS ↗

A clear process. From start to finish.

01

Confirm what must stay.

You send photographs and any required signs, and we record what must remain visible before design work starts.

02

Design in school colours.

Our designers match your crest and colours and show the layout on your minibus for the head, bursar or governors to approve.

03

Produce.

Panels are printed in-house on 8-colour, 1440dpi printers and lettering is cut from 3M and Metamark vinyl.

04

Fit on agreed dates.

The minibus is fitted at our Norwich workshop on dates agreed in advance, ideally outside term time.

Your questions. Answered.

Does our minibus need school bus signs?

It depends on how the vehicle is used, and rules can change. Check the current guidance with your local authority or transport provider. If signs are required, we will plan the layout so they have their own clear space.

Can you reproduce our school crest?

Yes. Send the crest in the best format you have. Vector files are ideal; if you only have a low-resolution version, our design department can discuss redrawing it for your approval.

Can graphics go on the windows?

They can, but we usually advise keeping passenger and driver glass clear for light and visibility. If you need window graphics, tell us which windows and why, and check the rules on driver visibility.

How much do minibus graphics cost?

Minibuses are quoted individually. As a guide, our van packages start from £149 + VAT for Basic graphics. Send photographs and your crest for a quote.

We’re replacing the minibus. Can the graphics move across?

Vinyl is applied to one vehicle and can’t be moved, but the approved design can be reused and adjusted to fit the new model.

Who, what and how to reach you.

People see a vehicle for a few seconds. A name, one line about what you do and a phone number or web address do most of the work.

Visible deterrent. Clear identity.

Security vehicles are read by two audiences. Clients and their tenants want reassurance that the patrol is real and comes from a professional firm. Anyone up to no good should see, from a distance and at night, that a security company is on site. Both need the same thing: a clear company name, a recognisable logo and a contact number.

There is a third audience to keep in mind: the public. Security livery must not suggest that the vehicle belongs to the police or an emergency service. That rules out battenburg and chequered patterns, police-style colour schemes, and words such as “Police” or wording that could be taken for an emergency service. Restrictions apply to emergency-style markings, so check the current rules before you design. We will not copy emergency-service livery, and we will say so if a design gets too close.

A strong, distinctive company look is the better answer. Your own colours, a bold name and well-placed reflective detail make the vehicle easy to identify without borrowing anyone else’s authority.

Booked by people who saw you last week.

Skip hire is a local, repeat-search business. A household clearing a garage or a builder starting an extension will often book the firm whose lorry they noticed on the next street, or whose skip sat on a neighbour’s drive. The graphics on a skip lorry are therefore less about image and more about recall: a name that sticks, the words “skip hire” so nobody has to guess, and a phone number that can be read in the few seconds the lorry takes to pass.

Many customers also want to know what you offer before they ring. A short line such as “Mini, midi & builders’ skips”, “Roll-on roll-off” or “Grab hire & muck-away” filters the calls you want. Opening the website or ringing should be the obvious next step, so the web address and number deserve generous sizes.

Hard-working bodies. Simple messages.

Tippers spend their days between quarries, merchants, building sites and tips, and most of their miles are on local roads where the same people see them again and again. The builder waiting for a load of type 1, the farmer who needs a muck-away and the homeowner ordering topsoil are all potential customers. The graphics need to say what you haul and how to order it, in lettering big enough to read on a vehicle that is moving or tipping on the far side of a site.

A short service line does a lot here: “Tipper hire”, “Aggregates delivered”, “Muck-away & grab hire”, “Muck-away & topsoil”. If you run under an owner-driver’s name, the name and number are often all a tipper needs. If you are a haulier with a mixed fleet, consistency between the tippers and your other vehicles makes the company look larger and better organised.

Typical vehicles range from 3.5-tonne tipper vans and pickups with tipping bodies, through 7.5- and 18-tonne rigids, to six- and eight-wheel tippers and articulated bulk tippers. The common thread is a steel body that takes a beating and a cab that stays relatively clean.

What goes where.

Layout

Cab for the brand. Body for the big number.

The cab carries the detail, because it is the panel least exposed to loading damage. The body sides are large and flat, which makes them ideal for a big name and phone number, kept low and clear of the top rail where buckets and grabs make contact.

Cab doors & sidesCompany name, logo and service line
Body sidesLarge name and phone number, below the top rail
Tailgate & rearName or number only, clear of lights, plates and markings

Sheeting systems, ladders and toolboxes all hide parts of the body. Photographs taken with the sheet in its travelling position help us place the lettering where it stays visible.

From door lettering to full livery.

Larger tippers are quoted for the vehicle and design. Tipper vans and pickups can often start from our published supply-and-fit packages, fitted within a 30-mile radius of the Norwich workshop. Prices are “from” and + VAT, and your quote confirms the figure for your vehicle.

Practical points for tippers.

Rear markings first. Larger goods vehicles carry rear markings and plates that are covered by regulations, and tippers working on the highway may also need chevrons. Check the current requirements for your vehicles and contracts, and keep anything required clear of graphics. Our highways & utilities page covers Chapter 8 kits.

Dust, mud and washing. Tippers get dirty fast and are washed hard. Edges of vinyl are the weak point, so ask your drivers to keep pressure-washer lances back from the graphics.

Body condition. Dented or rusting bodies give vinyl a poor surface. If a body is due a repaint, letter it afterwards; if not, keep the lettering to the soundest panels.

Leased cabs. If the tipper is leased or on finance, check what the agreement says about graphics and return condition before you book.

For tipper graphics, please send:

  • Photographs of both cab sides, both body sides and the tailgate, with the sheet in its travel position.
  • Any client vehicle specification or highways requirements you work to.

  • Exact wording: name, services, phone number and web address.
  • Where the vehicles are based, and whether they can come to our Norwich workshop.

Send photographs and the vehicle list. We can work with your designer or design from scratch.

Lettering placed low on the body sides, below the top rail, tends to last far better than anything near where loads are tipped in. We plan positions around how your tipper is loaded and sheeted.

Our van graphics, in 3M and Metamark materials, last up to 7 years if looked after correctly. On a tipper body, life depends on wear, washing and the condition of the steel.

Most trades and home-service businesses win work locally, and a large share of it comes from people who live near the jobs you are already doing. Parked outside the job, all day.

Tree work is one of the most visible trades there is. A crew might spend a full day at one property with a tipper, chipper and pickup lined up outside, while the whole street watches the canopy come down. That is when neighbours decide who to call about their own trees, so the vehicles should make it easy: a clear business name, what you do and a number that is simple to note down.

Arb customers are often cautious. They want to know you are qualified, insured and careful with their property. Graphics can’t prove that, but they can signal it: a tidy, consistent look across the vehicles, membership or approval logos you are entitled to use, and a web address where people can check your credentials.

Tree surgery vehicles also take punishment. Branches scrape the sides, chip and brash come over the tailgate and tipper bodies take knocks, so placement matters as much as design.

What goes where.

Layout

Cab for the name. Body for the number.

On a tipper, the cab doors are the safest place for the main branding: flat, at eye level and out of the way of the load. The tipper body and tailgate take knocks, so lettering there is best kept simple and easy to replace.

Cab doorsBusiness name and logo
Cab back or headboardName or web address, seen over the body
Tailgate or chipperPhone number, large and simple
Pickups and crew vansMatching name, trade line and contact details

Mesh-sided chip bodies can’t take vinyl directly. A rigid sign panel fixed to the body or headboard can carry the name instead; ask about it when you request a quote.

Your vehicle is the portfolio.

Valeting and detailing customers are buying a standard of finish, and they will look at your vehicle with the same eye. Peeling corners, faded print or crooked lettering undermine the message before you have unloaded the pressure washer. Graphics for this trade need clean edges, careful alignment and a design that suits the level of service you sell.

The message varies with the business. A mobile valeter doing maintenance washes on driveways needs to say “mobile” and show a booking number clearly. A detailer selling paint correction, ceramic coatings and colour-change work can afford a more striking design that shows off what vinyl and finishes can do, with less text and a strong web or social link to a portfolio.

Typical vehicles. Small and medium vans carrying a water tank, generator and pressure washer; estate cars towing a box trailer; and, for detailers, a demonstration car with a wrap, dechrome or a liquid-wrap finish to show at shows and on social media.

What goes where.

Layout

Name large. Services short. Booking clear.

On a van, the sides carry the name and “mobile valeting” or “detailing” message, with the booking number low down. On a car, the doors and bonnet do that job. A trailer’s large flat sides are ideal for a bold logo and web address, and they are often seen parked at the customer’s house for hours.

Sides / doorsName and what you offer
RearBooking phone, web and social handles
Trailer sidesLarge logo and web address
Demo carBrand, with the finish itself on show

If a water tank or pressure washer means the rear doors are open on the job, repeat the phone number on the sides so passers-by still see it.

Practical points for detailers.

Know your chemicals. You will understand this better than most. Strong solvents, tar removers and aggressive pre-washes can lift vinyl edges and dull printed laminate. Use gentle products on graphics and keep the pressure-washer lance well back from edges.

Matt and satin finishes. Matt and satin films need different care from gloss: no waxes or polishes that leave a shine, and no abrasive cloths. Ask us about aftercare for the finish you choose.

Water and weight. Tanks and kit make vans sit lower and doors work harder. Keep important graphics away from rear corners and step areas, where splashes and knocks are most frequent.

Show what you sell. If you offer wraps, dechrome or colour change yourself, your own car is the best advert. We can design it to show those finishes clearly in photographs.

Send us the following and we will come back with ideas and a quote:

How should I wash vehicle graphics?

Gently, by hand, with mild products. Avoid strong solvents on the vinyl and keep a pressure washer well back from edges. Matt and satin finishes need non-wax products.

A vinyl wrap is a film applied to the panels; liquid wrapping is sprayed on. Each suits different vehicles and finishes, so ask us to compare them for yours.

Growing a round, one street at a time.

Window cleaning works on rounds. You visit the same streets every few weeks, and much of your growth comes from the houses in between: people who see your van parked while you work next door and decide it is time to get someone in. The graphics need to tell them, in seconds, what you do and how to get on your round.

Many window cleaners now offer more than glass: gutter clearing, fascia and soffit cleaning, conservatory roofs, solar panels and softwashing. These are worth listing because customers rarely know who to call for them. Keep it to the three or four services that pay best, under a clear line such as “Window & gutter cleaning”.

Commercial customers matter too. Shops, offices and other premises often want a regular contractor who is plainly established and properly equipped, and a professional van with a water-fed pole system shows exactly that.

Typical window cleaning vehicles.

Small vansBerlingo, Partner or Caddy with a pure-water tank and hose reel
Medium vansFor larger tanks, several reels and longer poles
PickupsWith a tank system in the load bed

Water-fed pole systems change how a van is used. The tank and reel usually sit in the back, the rear doors are often open while you work, and poles ride on the roof.

Because the rear doors are often open for the hose reel, the side panels do most of the advertising while you work. We put the number on both sides in a large size, and repeat it on the rear doors for when you are driving.

Practical points for window cleaning vans.

Constant water. Your van is wet for much of the day. Vinyl copes with water, but edges last longer if you avoid aiming a pressure washer or hose jet at them.

Pole and ladder racks. Poles and ladders cover the top of the van. We keep lettering below the rack and design around rack feet and fixings.

How customers book. Many rounds are booked by text or message. If that is how you work, make the mobile number large, and only add “text to book” if you answer messages promptly.

New services. Adding solar panel cleaning or softwashing later is straightforward, because a line of vinyl can be added or replaced without redoing the van.

The ones that bring the most work beyond windows, such as gutters, fascias, conservatory roofs or solar panels. Three or four is plenty; customers can find the rest on your website.
